name: TRI-ME: trimetazidine for ME/CFS
title: Trimetazidine to treat ME/CFS: a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled efficacy trial
summary: Tests whether **trimetazidine**, a heart medicine that helps cells burn fuel more efficiently (approved for angina in Europe and Asia), improves ME/CFS symptoms. Participants take tablets for 8 weeks and complete questionnaires.
intervention: Trimetazidine 35 mg twice daily for 8 weeks vs placebo
locations: Barwon Health, Geelong VIC; Swinburne University, Hawthorn VIC
eligibility: Age 18+, meets the **Canadian Consensus Criteria** for ME/CFS, and has a current treating doctor. Not eligible: pregnancy or breastfeeding, severe kidney disease, Parkinson's or other movement disorders (including restless legs), MAOI medications, or being in another trial.
sponsor: Deakin University (IMPACT) · funded by the NHMRC
notes: Recruiting until 2029. Currently Victoria only. It's worth asking whether interstate participation is possible.

name: TreatMELC: low-dose naltrexone for ME/CFS and Long COVID
title: Low Dose Naltrexone for ME/CFS and Long COVID (Griffith University NCNED)
summary: A placebo-controlled trial of **low-dose naltrexone (LDN)** from Griffith University's NCNED, the team behind the TRPM3 ion channel research. It will also look at immune, ion channel and brain measures to find a treatment biomarker. Capsules are posted to participants.
intervention: LDN starting at 1.5 mg/day, increasing weekly to 4.5–6 mg/day, for 12 weeks vs placebo
locations: Recruiting from NSW, QLD and VIC
eligibility: Age 18–65, BMI 18.5–29.9. Either ME/CFS diagnosed by a doctor and meeting the Canadian and/or International Consensus Criteria, **or** Long COVID with brain fog, sleep problems and/or body pain. You're likely to be ineligible if you already take LDN.
sponsor: Griffith University · funded by the Stafford Fox Medical Research Foundation
notes: NCNED confirmed in September 2026 that this trial **hasn't started yet**. To hear when it opens, join the [NCNED research registry](https://redcap.link/NCNEDresearchregistry). The general NCNED line, (07) 5678 9283 or ncned@griffith.edu.au, can also help.

name: Griffith NCNED research studies & surveys
summary: Griffith University's National Centre for Neuroimmunology and Emerging Diseases runs a rolling programme of **mechanism studies** (blood tests of ion channels and genetics, brain MRI) and **online surveys** (quality of life, economic impact, gut symptoms). Some include free immune testing or MRI. **Join NCNED's research registry** (the "Study website" button) to be contacted about studies you may be eligible for.
intervention: Blood tests, MRI and surveys. No treatment.
eligibility: Usually age 18–60 or 18–65, Australian resident, non-smoker, not pregnant. People with ME/CFS, Long COVID or healthy volunteers, depending on the study.
notes: The research registry link was provided directly by NCNED (September 2026).

name: AusME Registry & Biobank
summary: Australia's national ME/CFS and Long COVID **registry and biobank**, run by Emerge Australia. You fill in online surveys every few months, with optional blood donation, and your data supports Australian research. More than 2,700 people have joined.
eligibility: Age 12+ living in Australia with ME/CFS or Long COVID, or healthy volunteers.
sponsor: Emerge Australia with La Trobe University
notes: When calling, **press 3** for research and biobank (Tue–Thu, 8am–3:30pm AEDT).

name: CNIC Study: brain inflammation imaging in ME/CFS (Sunshine Coast)
title: The Chronic Neuroinflammation in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) Study
summary: An Australian study using advanced **MRI** to look for signs of long-term brain inflammation in ME/CFS. It also measures the brain's waste-clearance (glymphatic) system and inflammation markers in blood. People with and without ME/CFS are needed.
intervention: None (observational): online questionnaires, one 40-minute MRI, blood and saliva samples, an optional 14-day activity monitor, and two telehealth interviews
locations: Thompson Institute, Birtinya, Sunshine Coast QLD (in person)
eligibility: Aged 18–65, with or without ME/CFS; able to communicate in English; no neurological or active psychiatric illness; able to have an MRI and give blood.
sponsor: University of the Sunshine Coast · Thompson Institute
contact_name: Register interest via the UniSC study page
notes: Participants receive $50 and an image of their brain scan. The MRI visit is in person, so plan rest around it.

name: NALCOVID: low-dose naltrexone for Long COVID
summary: Griffith University's placebo-controlled trial of LDN for Long COVID brain fog, sleep problems and pain. **People previously diagnosed with ME/CFS are excluded.**
intervention: LDN 1.5 mg/day, increasing to 4–6 mg/day, nightly for 12 weeks vs placebo
eligibility: Age 18–65 with Long COVID plus brain fog, sleep problems and/or body pain. **Excludes anyone diagnosed with ME/CFS.**
notes: The registry still says recruiting but hasn't been updated since June 2024, so recruitment has probably finished. Placebo participants can start LDN afterwards.

name: REVERSE-LC: baricitinib for Long COVID
summary: A large NIH-funded trial of **baricitinib**, an anti-inflammatory drug (JAK inhibitor), mainly for Long COVID thinking and memory problems. Researchers note that EBV reactivation is linked to Long COVID fatigue.
intervention: Baricitinib 4 mg daily for 24 weeks vs placebo
locations: 17 US sites including Vanderbilt, UCLA, UCSF, Yale, Emory and Brigham & Women's
eligibility: Age 18+, confirmed COVID infection at least 6 months ago, with Long COVID symptoms (mainly thinking and memory problems) for 6+ months that affect daily life. In-person visits required.
sponsor: Vanderbilt University Medical Center · NIH RECOVER-TLC
notes: Results expected 2027.

name: RECOVER-TLC: NIH Long COVID treatment trials
summary: The US National Institutes of Health programme of Long COVID treatment trials. REVERSE-LC (above) is enrolling now. Three more are **expected to open later in 2026**: **Brave-LC** (low-dose naltrexone, ages 6–25), **Tame-LC** (semaglutide) and **Block-LC** (stellate ganglion block).
eligibility: Depends on the trial. Full criteria for the three new trials haven't been published yet.

name: PIONEER: inebilizumab (B-cell depletion)
title: CD19 B-cell depletion with inebilizumab in PAIS-ME/CFS (Charité Berlin)
summary: Tests **inebilizumab**, which removes antibody-producing B cells, in people with ME/CFS who improved after immunoadsorption (blood filtering) and then relapsed. It tests the idea that autoantibodies drive the illness in some patients.
eligibility: Age 18–65, post-infectious ME/CFS with raised β2-adrenergic receptor autoantibodies. **Only people who took part in Charité's earlier immunoadsorption studies** and improved, then worsened.
notes: Expected to start December 2026.

name: PAIS-AriSE: low-dose aripiprazole
summary: The first placebo-controlled trial of **low-dose aripiprazole** (1 mg), after a Stanford clinic review suggested it helped fatigue, brain fog and sleep. For people with post-infectious syndromes, including post-COVID.
eligibility: Adults with a post-infectious syndrome or post-COVID condition for 3+ months, with neuropsychiatric symptoms such as brain fog. Excludes Bell score below 30, current antipsychotic use, or serious psychiatric illness in the past 10 years.
contact_name: PD Dr Christiana Franke; Dr Fabian Bösl
notes: Expected to start October 2026. ME/CFS isn't a formal entry requirement.

name: IMPACT: immunoadsorption in autoantibody-positive ME/CFS
summary: Follows people with post-infectious ME/CFS who test positive for certain autoantibodies and receive **immunoadsorption** (5 days of blood filtering to remove antibodies) as part of their care. This is the patient-selection approach researchers now favour.
intervention: Immunoadsorption as part of routine care
eligibility: Age 18–65, Canadian Consensus Criteria, PEM lasting 14+ hours, Bell score below 60, positive for certain autoantibodies, and immunoadsorption covered by German health insurance.
notes: Mainly relevant to people in Germany.

name: ACCESS: home-based care for housebound ME/CFS
summary: Tests **outreach care at home plus online visits** for people with severe ME/CFS who can't get to a clinic. It's one of very few studies designed for housebound and bedbound patients.
intervention: Home-based outreach care vs usual care
eligibility: Age 18–69, Canadian Consensus Criteria, **severe** (Bell score 30 or below), PEM over 14 hours.

name: MECFS-R: German ME/CFS registry
summary: A multi-centre registry of ME/CFS at **all ages**, including children, recording symptoms, course and care.
locations: MRI Chronic Fatigue Center for Young People, TU Munich
eligibility: Any age with an ME/CFS diagnosis based on international criteria.
notes: The registry record was last updated January 2025.

name: REenergizeME: intermittent hypoxia-hyperoxia (IHHT)
summary: Tests **breathing alternating low- and high-oxygen air** through a mask, a treatment designed to stimulate the cell's energy factories. Includes blood and skin samples to study how it works.
eligibility: **Women** aged 20–59 with mild or moderate ME/CFS (International Consensus Criteria) for 6+ months, with PEM. BMI 18–30. Severe ME/CFS excluded.
sponsor: Aarhus University · Independent Research Fund Denmark
notes: The planned June 2026 start has passed, so check the current status with the team.

name: PEM: a starting point to investigate ME/CFS
summary: Studies what happens in the body during **post-exertional malaise**, comparing people with ME/CFS and healthy controls.
eligibility: Age 18–65, International or Canadian Consensus Criteria, no immune-modulating drugs in the past 3 months.
notes: Studies of PEM usually involve an exertion task. Ask the team what's involved before agreeing.

name: HERITAGE: long-term follow-up of Long COVID and ME/CFS (UK)
summary: Follows people with Long COVID and/or ME/CFS for 12 months to compare NHS specialist services, using questionnaires (app or paper). You **don't need to be a clinic patient** to join.
intervention: Questionnaires on symptoms, quality of life and care
locations: Leeds, Leicester, Hertfordshire, Cornwall, plus a national remote group
eligibility: Adults 18+ with Long COVID or ME/CFS symptoms for more than 2 years. GP-diagnosed or self-reported is fine.
notes: Recruiting until December 2028.

name: Sequence ME & Long Covid
summary: The follow-on to DecodeME: reading the **full genomes** of up to 9,000 people with ME/CFS and 9,000 with Long COVID to find rare genetic variants.
eligibility: ME/CFS: **existing DecodeME participants only**. Long COVID: UK residents, criteria still being set.
sponsor: University of Edinburgh, EMBL-EBI, Action for ME · £4.75m UK government funding
notes: No new sign-ups for ME/CFS: the study will use samples already collected through DecodeME. The Long COVID arm isn't open yet; UK residents will be able to register interest once it is, and people outside the UK are unlikely to be eligible.

name: StudyME research registry (Open Medicine Foundation)
summary: A free **worldwide registry** that matches people with ME/CFS, Long COVID and related illnesses (and healthy volunteers) to studies that are recruiting. More than 15,000 people in 85 countries have signed up.
eligibility: Anyone with ME/CFS or a related illness, or healthy volunteers.
notes: A good way for people outside the US and Europe to hear about new studies.

name: LIFT: pyridostigmine + low-dose naltrexone
title: Life Improvement Trial
summary: Tests **pyridostigmine** and **LDN**, alone and together, in people with ME/CFS who also have orthostatic intolerance. The idea is to treat both circulation and immune/inflammation drivers.
intervention: Pyridostigmine and/or LDN vs placebo (four groups)
eligibility: Age 18–70, meets both IOM and Canadian criteria, with orthostatic intolerance; symptoms began before December 2023; no opioid use; needs a smartphone.
sponsor: Brigham and Women's Hospital · Open Medicine Foundation
notes: Recruiting until about September 2027; results expected after December 2027.

name: NIH brain imaging of pain and effort
summary: A brain-scan study at the NIH Clinical Center looking at how the brain processes **effort and unpleasant sensations** in ME/CFS.
intervention: fMRI during heat-pain and physical-effort tasks. No treatment.
eligibility: Age 18–50 with ME/CFS, or healthy controls. Must be able to travel to Bethesda.
notes: Includes effort tasks, so ask what's involved.

name: CHIIME: chronic infections and inflammation in ME/CFS
summary: Takes repeated samples over time to look for **infection and inflammation** drivers of ME/CFS, such as viral reactivation.
intervention: Blood and other samples. No treatment.
eligibility: Adults 18+ reporting an ME/CFS diagnosis, or healthy controls. Excludes HIV, hepatitis B or C, and severe anaemia.

name: Low-dose naltrexone dose-finding (UAB)
summary: Compares **four LDN doses** (1.5, 3, 4.5 and 6 mg) to find the best dose for ME/CFS. Run remotely by Dr Jarred Younger's lab.
eligibility: Age 18–65, **Alabama residents only**, International Consensus Criteria. Excludes opioid use, autoimmune disease and pregnancy.
notes: Planned start October 2026.

name: Voice analysis to diagnose and track ME/CFS (Mayo Clinic)
summary: Tests whether **smartphone voice recordings** can help diagnose and monitor ME/CFS. It's done entirely through an app, with no travel.
eligibility: Adults with ME/CFS confirmed by an ME/CFS specialist; smartphone, tablet or laptop.
notes: Remote, but check whether non-US participants are accepted.

name: Fareon magnetic device for brain fog (Mount Sinai)
summary: A pilot of a **head-worn microtesla magnetic device** used at home twice a week. An earlier randomised trial of the technology in Long COVID reported improved thinking and wellbeing.
phase: Open-label pilot, single group (target 30). Not a randomised trial.
eligibility: Age 16+, English-speaking, with at least mild thinking or memory problems linked to a confirmed diagnosis such as Long COVID. No cranial implants, pacemaker or seizure history.
sponsor: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
notes: ME/CFS is mentioned but isn't a formal entry requirement.

name: Lumbrokinase for Long COVID, post-Lyme and ME/CFS
summary: A pilot trial of **lumbrokinase**, an enzyme supplement thought to break down micro-clots, in three separate groups, one of which is ME/CFS.
eligibility: Adults with only one of Long COVID, post-treatment Lyme disease or ME/CFS, rating their current health 70/100 or lower.
sponsor: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai

name: Hydrogen water for ME/CFS (Stony Brook)
summary: A 16-week placebo-controlled trial of **molecular hydrogen** tablets dissolved in water, an antioxidant approach. Partly remote.
intervention: Hydrogen tablets in water vs placebo
locations: Stony Brook University, New York (partly remote)
eligibility: Age 18–65, meets ME/CFS criteria on a phone screen, has internet access. Excludes current or past depression.

name: Stanford ME/CFS imaging & biomarker studies
summary: Brain MRI, **whole-body PET/MRI** scans looking for inflammation (moderate to severe ME/CFS), and blood biomarker studies, from the team behind the 2026 muscle PET findings.
intervention: Imaging and blood tests. No treatment.
eligibility: Imaging: age 18–65, able to make two visits to Palo Alto (paid). Biomarker study: ME/CFS or Long COVID.
notes: Stanford's page is undated. Confirm the study is still open before travelling.

name: Bateman Horne Center biobank
summary: Collects saliva, blood and urine samples linked to clinical information, for ME/CFS, POTS and Long COVID research.
intervention: Samples at three visits, 3 months apart
locations: Bateman Horne Center, Salt Lake City, Utah
eligibility: People who have, or think they may have, ME/CFS. Three in-person visits needed.
notes: Recruitment has closed (confirmed by the Bateman Horne Center, October 2026). No date for results has been announced yet. BHC expects to start new research studies later in 2026.

name: Low-dose rapamycin study (Simmaron Research)
summary: Tracks symptoms and cell clean-up (autophagy) markers in patients whose own doctor prescribes **weekly low-dose rapamycin**. Early results: 74% of 70 patients improved (no placebo group). A placebo-controlled follow-up is planned for mid-2027.
locations: Palo Alto CA, Mayo Clinic MN, Incline Village NV, Bateman Horne Center UT, Seattle WA
eligibility: Must already be a patient of a participating clinician and be approved for rapamycin.
notes: Enrolment is by invitation through participating clinicians. Email trials@simmaron.com to ask about adding your clinician.

name: Blood-brain barrier study (Johns Hopkins)
summary: Uses brain imaging, cognitive tests and blood immune markers to test whether a **leaky blood-brain barrier** drives cognitive problems. It compares ME/CFS that began before COVID with ME/CFS that began after.
intervention: Imaging and blood tests. No treatment.
eligibility: Age 18–70, IOM 2015 criteria. Illness began before July 2019, or after a COVID infection.
notes: Invitation only, with no public contact.

name: MILES: online mind-body programme (Alberta)
summary: A randomised trial of the **Dynamic Neural Retraining System (DNRS)**, an online "brain retraining" programme, in Long COVID and ME/CFS.
eligibility: Adults with ME/CFS (IOM 2015) for 6+ months; internet access; English speaker.
notes: Brain-retraining programmes are **controversial** in the ME/CFS community. Listed for completeness; see [What to avoid](/treatment/avoid/#how-to-spot-hype).

name: STAR-CO: stellate ganglion block for Long COVID
summary: A single nerve-block injection in the neck vs a placebo injection, for Long COVID symptoms. **People with a prior ME or fibromyalgia diagnosis are excluded.**
intervention: Right stellate ganglion block vs saline injection
eligibility: Adults with Long COVID for 12+ weeks with breathlessness; must understand French. **Excludes diagnosed ME/CFS.**
notes: Not suitable for people with ME/CFS. Listed because stellate ganglion block is a treatment many people ask about.

name: Hyperbaric oxygen for ME/CFS (Israel)
summary: A sham-controlled trial of **60 hyperbaric oxygen sessions** over 3 months. It follows Charité's observation that benefit appeared only with more sessions.
locations: Sagol Center for Hyperbaric Medicine, Shamir Medical Center
eligibility: Adults with mild to moderate ME/CFS diagnosed 1+ years ago. Severe excluded. Many clinic visits needed.

name: Rituximab in ME/CFS (Japan)
summary: An exploratory placebo-controlled crossover trial of **rituximab**, a B-cell-depleting drug. A large Norwegian trial of rituximab was negative, but interest remains in autoimmune subgroups.
locations: National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry, Tokyo
eligibility: Age 18–65, Canadian criteria, performance status 4 or more, able to be admitted to hospital.
sponsor: National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry
notes: The registry was last updated April 2025.

name: Lingzhi (reishi) for ME/CFS or post-COVID fatigue
summary: A randomised trial of a **lingzhi mushroom capsule** compared with a waitlist.
locations: School of Chinese Medicine, University of Hong Kong
eligibility: Age 40–60 with CFS (broad Fukuda criteria) or post-COVID fatigue; no herbal medicine in the past 6 months.
notes: Uses a broad definition of CFS that doesn't require PEM.

name: RESETME: daratumumab (plasma-cell therapy)
summary: Tests **daratumumab**, which removes antibody-producing plasma cells, in moderate to severe ME/CFS. In the pilot, 6 of 10 people responded, some dramatically, and 5 stayed well 2–3 years later.
locations: Haukeland University Hospital, Bergen; Oslo University Hospital
eligibility: Age 18–64, Canadian criteria, moderate to severe, ill for 2+ years after an infection or immune trigger.
notes: **Closed to new applicants.** The hospital has long waiting lists and asks people not to send health information by email. Listed so you can follow the results.

name: STIMPACT: at-home ear vagus nerve stimulation
summary: A fully remote crossover trial comparing two types of **vagus nerve stimulation** through the ear, each used for 4 weeks at home.
eligibility: Age 18–65 with post-COVID syndrome and/or ME/CFS (Canadian criteria); German or English speaker.
notes: **Recruitment has closed.** Listed so you can follow the results.
